translations.text: And the chief eunuch gave them names: to Daniel, Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.
And Daniel said to Amelsad, whom the chief eunuch had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
And he listened to them and tested them for ten days.
And God gave them wisdom and understanding in all learning and wisdom, and Daniel understood every vision and dream.
And he said, “May the name of the Lord be blessed from eternity to eternity, for wisdom, understanding, and power belong to him.”
You, O king, were looking, and there was a statue, a great statue. Its face and its appearance were exceedingly dreadful, and it stood before you. The statue was exceedingly terrifying.
You watched until a stone was cut out without hands, and it struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and crushed them completely.
And the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay: one part of the kingdom will be strong, and part of it will be brittle.
When you hear the sound of the trumpet, pipe, drum, lyre, harp, the harmony of songs, and every kind of musical instrument, fall down and worship the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar set up.
To whom you promised to multiply their offspring like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore.
And it moved about, surrounding the furnace, and burned those of the Chaldeans whom it found.
For he rescued us from Hades and saved us from the hands of death.
After twelve months, while he was walking on the roof of his royal palace in Babylon.
They drank wine and praised the gods of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, but they did not praise the eternal God, who had authority over their souls.
At that very hour, the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall of the king’s palace, and the king saw the hand that was writing.
Tekel: it was weighed in the scales and found wanting.
And the king went to his house and lay down without supper, and no delicacies were brought before him, and sleep deserted him. And God shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not harm Daniel.

And the king gave an order, and they brought the men who had slandered Daniel and threw them into the lions’ den, along with their children and their wives. They had not yet reached the bottom of the den when the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
I, Daniel, after the first vision, was in Susa, in the citadel that is in the land of Elam, and I was beside the Ulai.
I lifted my eyes and saw, and there was a ram standing opposite the Ulai. Its horns were high, and one was higher than the other, and the higher one came up afterward.
And it came up to the horned ram that I had seen standing opposite the Ulai, and charged at it with all its strength.
As for its being broken and the other horns taking its place, four kings will arise from its nation, but not by their own power.
We have sinned, acted lawlessly, done wrong, rebelled, and turned away from your commandments and your ordinances.
Lord, shame belongs to our faces, to our kings, to our rulers, and to our fathers, for we have sinned.
And the Lord our God kept watch over our calamities and brought them upon us, for the Lord our God is righteous in all the deeds he has done to us, because we did not obey his voice.

Lord, in all your mercy, let your wrath turn away and your anger be lifted from your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain, for we have sinned, and because of our lawlessness and that of our fathers, Jerusalem and all your people have become a reproach to everyone around us.
And now, Lord our God, hear the prayers and petitions of your servant, and for your own sake show your face upon the sanctuary that has been laid waste.
And the king of the south will become strong, and one of the princes will become stronger than he and will exercise great dominion.
And the king of the south will come and heap up earth and capture fortified cities. The king’s forces will not stand firm, and his chosen men will rise up, but there will be no strength to stand.
And the hearts of both kings will be intent on evil, and they will speak lies at the same table, but it will not succeed, for the end is at the appointed times.
And he will stretch out his hand over the land, and the land of the Egyptians will not be delivered.
And blessed is the one who endures and reaches one thousand three hundred and thirty-five days.
